ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=90^\circ$, $BD$ bisects $\angle ABC$ and intersects $AC$ at point $D$, with $AB=4$, $BC=12$, $AD=3$. If point $P$ moves along $BC$, what is the minimum value of the length of segment $DP$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} When $DP \perp BC$, the length of the line segment $DP$ is minimized, \\
$\because BD$ bisects $\angle ABC$ and $\angle A = 90^\circ$, \\
when $DP \perp BC$, $DP = AD$, \\
$\because AD = 3$, \\
$\therefore$ the minimal value of $DP$ is $\boxed{3}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is on the left, and C is at the lower right; there is a right-angle mark at A, indicating AB⊥AC. Point D is located on side AC, line segment BD connects from B to D; point P is located on BC, and the figure draws the line segment DP from D toward the direction of BC. Then reason: When point P moves on line BC, the minimum value of DP is the perpendicular distance from point D to BC, namely take P as the foot of the perpendicular from D to BC. Because D is on the angle bisector BD of ∠ABC, the perpendicular distances from D to the two sides BA and BC of the angle are equal. Also because AB⊥AC and D is on AC, DA⊥AB, so the perpendicular distance from point D to BA is AD. It is known that AD=3, therefore the perpendicular distance from point D to BC is also equal to 3. Thus the minimum value of DP is 3.
